Name: a3_conditional_calibration_checks_v2
Title: Calibration and downstream checks for A3 conditional algebra with repeated stochastic trials
Short Hypothesis: A3 conditional algebra can be implemented with explicit failure controls, and its branch/residual bounds are calibrated across seeds and small downstream linearized SLAM fixtures; any practical gain is measured rather than assumed.
Related Work: SOM means subspace-based optimization, not self-organizing maps. Generic projection, gain closure, dual residual methods, and bootstrap calibration are prior art. Parent owns literature and scientific judgment; this revision does not claim novelty.
Abstract: This revision keeps the completed deterministic B1-B4 identity checks as a frozen baseline and extends them into a small empirical study. It adds 50-seed stochastic trials with bootstrap intervals, a condition-number sweep for near-singular linearized systems, and two toy linearized pose-graph/bundle-adjustment tasks. The goal is to test whether the A3 conditional branch/residual bounds are calibrated beyond a single Gaussian fixture and whether full A3 conditional corrections improve downstream end-point error relative to LS/ridge. No global novelty, real 3D SLAM, or SOM-performance claim is made.

datasets: deterministic complex linear systems and Gaussian validation fixtures from completed B1-B4
50-seed Gaussian and heavy-tailed residual fixtures with 2000 draws per seed
condition-number sweep ensemble of complex linear systems with known ground truth
two small linearized pose-graph/bundle-adjustment tasks with synthetic noisy observations
baselines: correct vs omitted residual derivative (frozen control)
plug-in theorem bound vs bootstrap percentile interval
full A3 conditional correction vs A3 without dual-residual correction
A3 conditional subspace projection vs unregularized least squares vs ridge-regularized least squares
fixed-chart vs moving-chart formula under near-degenerate charts
metrics: deterministic identity errors and expected-fail control statuses
empirical selection risk, coverage probability, and interval width across seeds
downstream root-mean-square endpoint/landmark error and failure rate
negative control violations and undercoverage flags
Experiments.compute_estimate: single CPU thread, pinned venv, small NumPy/SciPy arrays; 50 seeds x 2000 draws, condition sweep, two toy tasks; roughly 2-4 CPU hours.
steps: Reuse completed regenerate_checks.py and checks.json as a frozen baseline
Add seed-swept stochastic residual fixtures and bootstrap percentile intervals for branch bounds
Add condition-number sweep and two small linearized pose-graph/bundle-adjustment downstream tasks
Run full A3 conditional correction, no dual-residual ablation, and LS/ridge baselines
Audit deterministic expected-fail controls and summarize calibration/downstream findings

Risk Factors and Limitations: Synthetic and toy-linearized settings only; no real 3D or full SLAM evidence
Bootstrap intervals are approximate finite-sample calibrations, not proof
Downstream tasks may show no practical advantage; this would be recorded as a negative result
Parent must independently audit; no global candidate coverage or SOM performance claim
